answer.origin: NVIDIA representative, in a statement to Tom’s Hardware on 2026-07-06.
answer.note: NVIDIA’s representative said, “Our roadmap is intact,” in the context of Tom’s Hardware’s report about alleged Kyber delays and changes to related products. This is NVIDIA’s broad, dated characterization of its roadmap, but the representative provided no further details. It is a counterpoint to the specific claims relayed from SemiAnalysis that Kyber NVL144 was delayed to 2028, NVL72x2 was scrapped, the four-die Rubin Ultra was canceled, and CPO-NVSwitch would arrive later (e49, e51, e53, e54); those remain reported claims, not established facts here. If “intact” means the reported changes do not reflect NVIDIA’s actual product plans, that would reduce concern about disruption to its planned Data Center products. The statement does not specify affected products, timing, deployments, or any FY2027 revenue implications, so it does not settle those questions.
limitations: NVIDIA did not clarify which products or milestones it meant by “roadmap,” or address the reported Kyber, NVL72x2, Rubin Ultra, or CPO-NVSwitch claims individually.
The statement provides no schedule, deployment, customer, or revenue information that would quantify an effect on FY2027 Data Center revenue.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA’s subsequent official product-roadmap disclosures and statements for specific confirmation or correction of the Kyber, NVL72x2, Rubin Ultra, and CPO-NVSwitch timing claims.
Check later NVIDIA guidance and FY2027 results for disclosed product timing, deployments, or Data Center revenue effects.
